subject: Model mix & pricing follow-up: token volumes & unit economics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@brightlayer.com>, Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 05 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Model mix & pricing follow-up: token volumes & unit economics

Hi Ethan / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few follow-ups so we can get you an accurate proforma: 

What I heard on the call (please confirm):
- Primary product: in-app assistant (chat) powering contextual replies and multi-turn flows.
- Secondary usages: embeddings for semantic search + reranking for result tuning.
- Expected steady-state volume (monthly): chat ~120M tokens, embeddings ~8M vector calls (approx. equivalent to ~12M tokens), rerank ~5M tokens.
- Desired go-live: pilot in Q1; production by end of Q1 if pilot meets latency and cost targets.
- Target blended unit economics target you mentioned on the call: roughly $250–$350 per 1M tokens blended.

Questions / asks from our side to finalize pricing scenarios:
1) Can you confirm the monthly volumes above and whether the embeddings number should be counted as vector calls or tokens (we can model both; embeddings are often priced differently in practice).
2) Any constraints on latency (p50/p95) for chat and rerank? This affects whether we suggest dedicated capacity vs shared hosted.
3) Do you have a preferred model mix (e.g., high-quality chat model for 80% of traffic and a smaller, cheaper variant for batched/background ops), or are you targeting a single model family for uniformity?

Attached is a lightweight pricing proforma (RIF-pricing-proforma.xlsx) with placeholders for the numbers we discussed. I filled in a baseline scenario assuming chat = 75% token share, embeddings = 15%, rerank = 10%.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the monthly volumes (or send a rough monthly token CSV)
- We run a 2-week pilot (sample traffic + performance run) and supply a detailed cost/latency report
- If the pilot looks good, we prepare a reserved capacity offer for predictable unit economics

Will follow up with Dev and David on the best pilot configuration (quantization options, model variants to test).

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0198

Date: Wed, 06 Dec 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model mix & pricing follow-up: token volumes & unit economics

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap. Quick confirmations and a few notes inline: 

On Tue, Dec 5, 2026 at 4:12 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference> wrote:
> - Expected steady-state volume (monthly): chat ~120M tokens, embeddings ~8M vector calls (approx. equivalent to ~12M tokens), rerank ~5M tokens.

Those figures look right for steady-state. To be explicit: our product team thinks monthly averages will be closer to chat = 130M tokens, embeddings = 10M vector calls, rerank = 6M tokens (there's some seasonality).

Regarding target unit economics — we were hoping to see a blended target of ~ $300 / 1M tokens. We understand embeddings may be priced differently; for budgeting purposes treat embeddings as equivalent to tokens for now.

Latency: p50 chat 120ms, p95 chat 800ms (soft); rerank ideally < 200ms p95. If dedicated capacity is required to hit p95 targets we can discuss that in the pilot scope.

A couple of asks from BrightLayer for the proforma: 
- Please provide a scenario showing (a) hosted shared model (pay-as-you-go), (b) dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) and (c) a quantized model variant that reduces cost by ~30% but adds ~10–15% latency.
- Can you show a target $/1M tokens that gets us to a monthly spend in the range of $35k–$45k for the volumes above? That helps our finance team.

If you can send an updated proforma with those scenarios I can loop in procurement next week. Happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

—Ethan
Ethan Shaw | Dir. Product, BrightLayer
ethan.shaw@brightlayer.com | +1 (212) 555-0147

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@brightlayer.com>, Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 06 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model mix & pricing follow-up: token volumes & unit economics

Ethan — thanks, this is super helpful. Attached is a short PDF that lays out three scenarios (hosted, dedicated reserve, quantized variant) using the updated volumes you provided: chat 130M, embeddings (modeled as 10M token-equivalent), rerank 6M.

High-level unit economics (example assumptions shown in PDF):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go) blended: $340 / 1M tokens (chat: $360, embeddings: $220, rerank: $300)
- Dedicated reserved (monthly commit): blended: $265 / 1M tokens (chat: $280, embeddings: $180, rerank: $240)
- Quantized model variant (dedicated + 8–12% latency penalty, ~30% cost reduction): blended: $185 / 1M tokens

Using the volumes you confirmed (chat 130M + embeddings 10M + rerank 6M = ~146M tokens total), monthly spend examples: 
- Hosted: 146 * $340 / 1M => ~$49.6k/month
- Dedicated: 146 * $265 / 1M => ~$38.7k/month
- Quantized dedicated: 146 * $185 / 1M => ~$27.0k/month

So to hit BrightLayer's target of $35k–$45k we would recommend the Dedicated reserved scenario at the $265 blended level (or a mixed approach: dedicated for high-volume chat with hosted fallbacks for lower-priority traffic).

Notes on model mix and testing:
- Recommend piloting two chat model variants: a higher-capacity model for 80% of sessions and a cost-optimized variant for background/batch tasks. That typically yields a ~10–15% cost improvement vs a single-model approach while preserving UX quality.
- For embeddings we recommend the standard 1536-d vector model for recall; we can test a smaller 768-d model in the pilot to measure quality delta vs cost.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Dev and David will propose a pilot config (instance sizes, quantized vs fp16, sample traffic generation).
2) I will update the XLS proforma with the dedicated pricing rows and send to you by EOD.
3) If that looks good, can you share the procurement contact so we can start a preliminary SOW/commit schedule?

Attaching: RIF-scenario-breakdown.pdf (scenarios + monthly cost table).

Thanks —
Marissa
